subject: Physics
text_content: The first law of thermodynamics states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted from one form to another. Mathematically, ΔU = Q − W, where ΔU is the change in internal energy, Q is the heat added to the system, and W is the work done by the system.

subject: Physics
text_content: An isothermal process is one in which the temperature of the system remains constant. For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal expansion, the work done is W = nRT ln(V₂/V₁). Since temperature is constant, ΔU = 0 and Q = W.

subject: Physics
text_content: An adiabatic process is one in which no heat is exchanged with the surroundings (Q = 0). For an ideal gas, the relationship between pressure and volume is PV^γ = constant, where γ = Cp/Cv is the heat capacity ratio.

subject: Physics
text_content: Carnot's theorem states that no heat engine operating between two heat reservoirs can be more efficient than a Carnot engine operating between the same temperatures. The Carnot efficiency is η = 1 − T_cold/T_hot.

subject: Physics
text_content: Entropy is a measure of the disorder or randomness in a system. The second law of thermodynamics states that the total entropy of an isolated system always increases or remains constant. For a reversible process, ΔS = Q_rev/T.

subject: Physics
text_content: The zeroth law of thermodynamics states that if two systems are in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other. This forms the basis for temperature measurement.

subject: Physics
text_content: The coefficient of performance (COP) of a refrigerator is the ratio of heat removed from the cold reservoir to the work done. COP_refrigerator = Q_cold / W = T_cold / (T_hot − T_cold) for a Carnot refrigerator.

subject: Physics
text_content: In a PV diagram, the area enclosed by a cyclic process represents the net work done by the system. Clockwise cycles represent engines (net positive work output), while counterclockwise cycles represent refrigerators (net positive work input).

subject: Physics
text_content: The specific heat capacity of a substance is the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of the substance by 1°C. For water, C_p ≈ 4186 J/(kg·K). For gases, we distinguish between C_p (at constant pressure) and C_v (at constant volume), with C_p − C_v = R for ideal gases.

subject: Physics
text_content: Stefan-Boltzmann Law: Every object emits thermal radiation. The power radiated per unit area is P/A = εσT⁴, where ε is the emissivity (0 to 1), σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W/(m²·K⁴) is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant, and T is the absolute temperature.

subject: Physics
text_content: Snell's Law describes the refraction of light at an interface: n₁ sin(θ₁) = n₂ sin(θ₂), where n₁ and n₂ are the refractive indices of the two media, and θ₁ and θ₂ are the angles of incidence and refraction with respect to the normal.

subject: Physics
text_content: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a denser to a rarer medium at an angle greater than the critical angle. The critical angle θ_c satisfies sin(θ_c) = n₂/n₁ (where n₁ > n₂). Optical fibres use this principle.

subject: Physics
text_content: The lens formula is 1/f = 1/v − 1/u, where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance (using the sign convention where distances are measured from the optical centre).

subject: Physics
text_content: Young's Double Slit Experiment demonstrates the wave nature of light. Constructive interference occurs at path difference = mλ, and destructive interference at (m + 1/2)λ. Fringe width β = λD/d, where D is the slit-to-screen distance and d is the slit separation.

subject: Physics
text_content: The resolving power of a microscope is defined by the Rayleigh criterion: the minimum resolvable distance is d = 0.61λ/n·sin(α), where λ is the wavelength of light, n is the refractive index of the medium, and α is the half-angle of the objective lens.

subject: Physics
text_content: Huygen's Principle states that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets. The new wavefront is the envelope of all these secondary wavelets. This principle explains reflection, refraction, and diffraction.

subject: Physics
text_content: In single-slit diffraction, the condition for minima is a·sin(θ) = mλ (m = ±1, ±2, ...), where a is the slit width and λ is the wavelength. The central maximum has an angular width of 2λ/a.

subject: Physics
text_content: Newton's second law in rotational form: τ = Iα, where τ is the net torque, I is the moment of inertia, and α is the angular acceleration. This is the rotational analogue of F = ma.

subject: Physics
text_content: The moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its diameter is I = (2/5)mr². For a hollow sphere it is I = (2/3)mr². For a solid cylinder about its axis, I = (1/2)mr².

subject: Physics
text_content: The work-energy theorem states that the net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy: W_net = ΔKE = (1/2)mv₂² − (1/2)mv₁².

subject: Physics
text_content: In simple harmonic motion (SHM), the restoring force is proportional to displacement: F = −kx. The period of oscillation is T = 2π√(m/k) for a spring-mass system and T = 2π√(L/g) for a simple pendulum.

subject: Physics
text_content: Escape velocity from a planet is the minimum speed needed to break free from its gravitational pull without further propulsion: v_e = √(2GM/R), where G is the gravitational constant, M is the planet's mass, and R is its radius.

subject: Physics
text_content: For circular motion, the centripetal acceleration is a = v²/r = ω²r, directed towards the centre. The centripetal force is F = mv²/r = mω²r.

subject: Physics
text_content: Conservation of angular momentum: when no external torque acts on a system, L = Iω = constant. This explains why a spinning ice skater spins faster when pulling in their arms.

subject: Physics
text_content: Bernoulli's principle states that for an ideal fluid in steady flow, the sum P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant along a streamline. This explains why pressure decreases as fluid speed increases.

subject: Physics
text_content: Gauss's Law states that the total electric flux through a closed surface is equal to the enclosed charge divided by ε₀: Φ_E = Q_enc/ε₀. This is used to find electric fields for symmetric charge distributions.

subject: Physics
text_content: Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction: the induced EMF in a loop is equal to the negative rate of change of magnetic flux through it: ε = −dΦ_B/dt. This is the basis for electric generators.

subject: Physics
text_content: Lenz's Law states that the induced current in a conductor opposes the change in magnetic flux that caused it. This is consistent with the law of conservation of energy.

subject: Physics
text_content: Ampere's Circuital Law: the line integral of the magnetic field around a closed loop equals μ₀ times the total current enclosed by that loop: ∮B·dl = μ₀I_enc.

subject: Physics
text_content: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is C = ε₀A/d, where A is the plate area and d is the separation. With a dielectric (κ) inserted, C = κε₀A/d. Energy stored is U = Q²/(2C) = CV²/2.

subject: Physics
text_content: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) states that the algebraic sum of all voltages around any closed loop in a circuit is zero. Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) states that the sum of currents entering a node equals the sum leaving it.

subject: Physics
text_content: The photoelectric effect: when light of frequency f strikes a metal surface, electrons are emitted only if f ≥ f₀ (threshold frequency). The maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is KE_max = hf − φ, where φ = hf₀ is the work function.

subject: Physics
text_content: de Broglie's hypothesis: every moving particle has an associated wavelength λ = h/mv = h/p. This wave-particle duality was confirmed by the Davisson-Germer electron diffraction experiment.

subject: Physics
text_content: Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom: electrons orbit in discrete energy levels. The energy of the nth level is E_n = −13.6/n² eV. Transitions emit photons with energy ΔE = hf = E_higher − E_lower.

subject: Physics
text_content: Radioactive decay law: N(t) = N₀ e^(−λt), where λ is the decay constant. The half-life T₁/₂ = ln2/λ. Activity A = λN. Types of decay: alpha (²₂He nucleus), beta (electron/positron), gamma (high-energy photon).

subject: Chemistry
text_content: SN2 reactions proceed via a single concerted step: the nucleophile attacks from the back, inverting the stereochemistry (Walden inversion). The rate = k[substrate][nucleophile]. Primary alkyl halides favour SN2.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: SN1 reactions proceed in two steps: (1) slow ionisation to form a carbocation intermediate, (2) fast attack by the nucleophile. Rate = k[substrate]. Tertiary alkyl halides favour SN1 and give racemic mixtures.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: In electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS), an electrophile replaces a hydrogen on the benzene ring. Examples: nitration (NO₂⁺), sulfonation (SO₃), halogenation (with Lewis acid catalyst), Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Markovnikov's Rule: in electrophilic addition of HX to an unsymmetrical alkene, the hydrogen adds to the carbon with more hydrogens. Equivalently, the carbocation intermediate that forms is the more stable one.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Aldol condensation: an alpha-carbon of one carbonyl compound acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbonyl carbon of another. The product is a β-hydroxy aldehyde or ketone. Under heating, dehydration gives the α,β-unsaturated product.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Grignard reagents (RMgX) are strong nucleophiles and bases. They react with aldehydes to give secondary alcohols, with ketones to give tertiary alcohols, and with CO₂ to give carboxylic acids.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: The mechanism of ester hydrolysis (acid-catalysed): (1) protonation of carbonyl oxygen, (2) nucleophilic attack by water, (3) proton transfer, (4) elimination of alcohol, (5) deprotonation to give carboxylic acid.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Hofmann rearrangement: primary amides react with Br₂ in alkaline solution to give primary amines with one fewer carbon. The nitrene intermediate undergoes migration: RCONH₂ → RNH₂.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Le Chatelier's Principle: if a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it will shift to counteract the disturbance and re-establish equilibrium. Increasing concentration of a reactant shifts the equilibrium to the right.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: The equilibrium constant K_c = [products]^stoich / [reactants]^stoich. It is temperature-dependent only. K_p = K_c(RT)^Δn, where Δn is the change in moles of gas.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Van't Hoff equation relates K to temperature: d(lnK)/dT = ΔH°/RT². For an exothermic reaction, increasing temperature decreases K (shifts equilibrium left).

subject: Chemistry
text_content: The degree of dissociation α and equilibrium constant are related. For A ⇌ B + C with initial concentration C₀: K = α²C₀/(1 − α). When α ≪ 1, α ≈ √(K/C₀).

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Buffer solutions resist changes in pH. The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]). Buffers work best when pH ≈ pKa (within ±1 unit).

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Solubility product K_sp = [M^m+]^m[X^n-]^n for the salt M_m X_n. Common ion effect: adding a common ion decreases solubility. For complex equilibria, successive stability constants are used.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: The Nernst equation relates cell potential to concentration: E = E° − (RT/nF)ln(Q), or at 25°C: E = E° − (0.0592/n)log(Q). At equilibrium, E = 0 and Q = K, giving ΔG° = −nFE° = −RTlnK.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Faraday's laws of electrolysis: (1) The mass deposited is proportional to the quantity of charge passed. (2) For the same charge, masses deposited are proportional to their equivalent weights. m = MIt/(nF).

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Standard electrode potentials are measured relative to the Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE, E° = 0 V). A positive E° means the half-reaction proceeds spontaneously as a reduction vs. SHE.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Kohlrausch's law of independent migration: the molar conductivity at infinite dilution Λ°_m = λ°_+ + λ°_−. This allows calculation of Λ°_m for weak electrolytes that cannot be measured directly.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: VSEPR theory predicts molecular geometry based on minimising repulsion between electron pairs around the central atom. Lone pairs occupy more space than bond pairs. Linear (2 BP), trigonal planar (3 BP), tetrahedral (4 BP).

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Molecular orbital (MO) theory: atomic orbitals combine to form bonding and antibonding MOs. Bond order = (bonding electrons − antibonding electrons)/2. O₂ has bond order 2 and is paramagnetic (two unpaired electrons in π* MOs).

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Hybridisation: sp (linear, 180°), sp² (trigonal planar, 120°), sp³ (tetrahedral, 109.5°), sp³d (trigonal bipyramidal), sp³d² (octahedral). The hybridisation determines the geometry of the σ-bonding framework.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Hydrogen bonding is the electrostatic attraction between a highly electronegative atom (O, N, F) covalently bonded to H and another electronegative atom. It explains the anomalously high boiling point of water and the structure of DNA.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Crystal Field Theory (CFT) explains the splitting of d-orbitals in transition metal complexes. In an octahedral field, d-orbitals split into lower t₂g (3 orbitals) and higher eₘ (2 orbitals) sets, with a splitting energy Δ_o.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: The spectrochemical series ranks ligands by their ability to split d-orbitals: I⁻ < Br⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < H₂O < NH₃ < en < CN⁻ < CO. Strong-field ligands cause low-spin configurations; weak-field ligands cause high-spin.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Effective Atomic Number (EAN) rule: stable complexes tend to have the central metal atom with 18 electrons (filled valence shell), analogous to the noble gas configuration.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Integration by parts: ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du. Choose u and dv using LIATE (Logarithmic, Inverse trig, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential) to simplify the integral.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: if F'(x) = f(x), then ∫[a to b] f(x)dx = F(b) − F(a). The derivative of ∫[a to x] f(t)dt with respect to x is f(x).

subject: Mathematics
text_content: L'Hôpital's Rule: if lim f(x)/g(x) is of the form 0/0 or ∞/∞ as x → c, then lim f(x)/g(x) = lim f'(x)/g'(x), provided the latter limit exists.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Taylor series expansion of f(x) about x = a: f(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x−a) + f''(a)(x−a)²/2! + ... = Σ f^(n)(a)(x−a)^n/n!. For Maclaurin series, a = 0.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: The chain rule for differentiation: if y = f(g(x)), then dy/dx = f'(g(x)) · g'(x). For implicit differentiation, differentiate both sides with respect to x and solve for dy/dx.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Partial fractions decomposition is used to integrate rational functions. For repeated linear factors (x−a)^n, include terms A₁/(x−a) + A₂/(x−a)² + ... + Aₙ/(x−a)^n. For irreducible quadratic factors ax²+bx+c, include (Ax+B)/(ax²+bx+c).

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Definite integration using substitution: when substituting u = g(x), change the limits of integration accordingly to x = a → u = g(a) and x = b → u = g(b).

subject: Mathematics
text_content: The general equation of a conic section is Ax² + Bxy + Cy² + Dx + Ey + F = 0. The discriminant B² − 4AC determines the type: < 0 (ellipse), = 0 (parabola), > 0 (hyperbola).

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Parametric form of an ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1: x = a·cos(t), y = b·sin(t). The eccentricity e = c/a where c² = a² − b² (a > b). Foci at (±c, 0).

subject: Mathematics
text_content: For a parabola y² = 4ax: focus at (a, 0), directrix x = −a, vertex at origin. The distance from any point P on the parabola to the focus equals its distance to the directrix (definition).

subject: Mathematics
text_content: The equation of a tangent to the circle x² + y² = r² at point (x₁, y₁) is xx₁ + yy₁ = r². For the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 at (x₁, y₁): xx₁/a² + yy₁/b² = 1.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: The angle between two lines with slopes m₁ and m₂ is tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)|. Lines are perpendicular when m₁m₂ = −1; parallel when m₁ = m₂.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Binomial Theorem: (a + b)^n = Σ C(n,r) a^(n−r) b^r for r = 0 to n. The general term T_(r+1) = C(n,r) a^(n−r) b^r. The middle term exists when n is even.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Quadratic equations ax² + bx + c = 0 have roots α, β where α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a (Vieta's formulas). Discriminant D = b² − 4ac: D > 0 (real distinct), D = 0 (equal), D < 0 (complex).

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Arithmetic Progression (AP): a, a+d, a+2d, ... The nth term aₙ = a + (n−1)d. Sum of n terms Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n−1)d] = n/2 [first + last term].

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Geometric Progression (GP): a, ar, ar², ... The nth term aₙ = ar^(n−1). Sum Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1) for r ≠ 1. Sum to infinity S_∞ = a/(1−r) for |r| < 1.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Permutations and combinations: P(n,r) = n!/(n−r)! (ordered), C(n,r) = n!/[r!(n−r)!] (unordered). Multinomial: arrange n objects of which p are identical, q identical, ... in n!/(p!q!...) ways.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Complex numbers: z = a + bi where i² = −1. Modulus |z| = √(a²+b²), argument θ = arctan(b/a). Euler's formula: e^(iθ) = cos θ + i·sin θ. De Moivre's theorem: (cos θ + i sin θ)^n = cos(nθ) + i sin(nθ).

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Bayes' Theorem: P(A|B) = P(B|A)·P(A) / P(B). This updates prior probability P(A) with evidence B to give the posterior P(A|B). Widely used in Bayesian inference and classification.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: The binomial distribution models the number of successes in n independent Bernoulli trials: P(X = k) = C(n,k) p^k (1−p)^(n−k). Mean = np, Variance = np(1−p).

subject: Mathematics
text_content: The normal distribution N(μ, σ²) has PDF f(x) = (1/σ√(2π)) exp(−(x−μ)²/2σ²). The 68-95-99.7 rule: 68% of data lies within ±1σ, 95% within ±2σ, 99.7% within ±3σ of the mean.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Covariance Cov(X,Y) = E[(X−μ_X)(Y−μ_Y)]. Correlation ρ = Cov(X,Y)/(σ_X σ_Y), ranging from −1 to +1. Correlation of 0 implies no linear relationship, not independence.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Determinant of a 3×3 matrix by cofactor expansion along the first row: det(A) = a₁₁M₁₁ − a₁₂M₁₂ + a₁₃M₁₃, where M_ij is the minor (determinant of the 2×2 matrix obtained by deleting row i and column j).

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Eigenvalues λ of matrix A satisfy det(A − λI) = 0. Eigenvectors v satisfy (A − λI)v = 0. Eigendecomposition: A = PDP⁻¹ where D is diagonal with eigenvalues and P has corresponding eigenvectors as columns.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: The cross product of vectors a × b is perpendicular to both a and b, with magnitude |a||b|sin θ. Using the right-hand rule gives the direction. a × b = (a₂b₃ − a₃b₂, a₃b₁ − a₁b₃, a₁b₂ − a₂b₁).

subject: Biology
text_content: Mendel's Law of Segregation: each organism carries two alleles for each trait, and these separate during gamete formation. Each gamete receives only one allele. This explains the 3:1 phenotypic ratio in F2 crosses.

subject: Biology
text_content: Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment: alleles for different traits segregate independently of one another during gamete formation, provided the genes are on different chromosomes (not linked).

subject: Biology
text_content: Incomplete dominance: the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype (e.g., red × white → pink). Codominance: both alleles are fully expressed (e.g., A and B blood types, giving AB). Both violate simple dominance.

subject: Biology
text_content: Sex-linked inheritance: genes on the X chromosome are said to be X-linked. Males (XY) express X-linked recessive traits more often than females (XX) because they have only one X. Examples: haemophilia, colour blindness.

subject: Biology
text_content: DNA replication is semi-conservative: each new double helix consists of one original strand and one new strand. The enzyme DNA polymerase III extends the new strand 5' → 3', using the original strand as template.

subject: Biology
text_content: Crossing over (recombination) occurs during prophase I of meiosis at chiasmata. It increases genetic variation and causes linked genes to be inherited separately. Recombination frequency is used to construct genetic maps (1 cM = 1% recombination).

subject: Biology
text_content: The fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane: phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins. Cholesterol regulates fluidity. Integral proteins span the membrane; peripheral proteins are on the surface.

subject: Biology
text_content: Active transport moves ions against their concentration gradient using energy (ATP). The Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase pump moves 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in per ATP hydrolysed, maintaining the resting membrane potential.

subject: Biology
text_content: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells. Phases: Prophase (chromatin condenses, spindle forms), Metaphase (chromosomes align at plate), Anaphase (sister chromatids separate), Telophase & Cytokinesis.

subject: Biology
text_content: Meiosis produces four genetically diverse haploid cells (gametes). Key features: meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes (reductional division); meiosis II separates sister chromatids (similar to mitosis).

subject: Biology
text_content: The endomembrane system includes the ER, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, and vesicles. Rough ER (with ribosomes) synthesises secretory and membrane proteins; smooth ER synthesises lipids and detoxifies.

subject: Biology
text_content: Transcription produces mRNA from DNA template (3'→5' strand read; mRNA is 5'→3'). RNA polymerase II transcribes protein-coding genes. Promoter sequences (TATA box) and transcription factors direct initiation.

subject: Biology
text_content: Translation: the ribosome reads mRNA in the 5'→3' direction, three nucleotides (codon) at a time. tRNA with matching anticodon delivers the amino acid. Start codon AUG (Met); stop codons UAA, UAG, UGA.

subject: Biology
text_content: PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) amplifies specific DNA sequences: (1) Denaturation at 94°C — strands separate, (2) Annealing at ~55°C — primers bind, (3) Extension at 72°C — Taq polymerase extends. Each cycle doubles the copies.

subject: Biology
text_content: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing: Cas9 endonuclease guided by a single-guide RNA (sgRNA) creates a double-strand break at the target sequence. Non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) causes insertions/deletions; homology-directed repair (HDR) enables precise edits.

subject: Biology
text_content: Restriction enzymes (endonucleases) cut double-stranded DNA at specific palindromic recognition sequences. EcoRI cuts at 5'–GAATTC–3'. Restriction digestion + gel electrophoresis is used to fingerprint DNA.

subject: Biology
text_content: The carbon cycle: carbon enters ecosystems through photosynthesis (CO₂ → organic compounds) and is released by respiration, decomposition, and combustion. Ocean absorption, weathering, and volcanic activity also play roles.

subject: Biology
text_content: The nitrogen cycle: atmospheric N₂ is fixed by Rhizobium bacteria (associated with legumes) and Azotobacter. Ammonia is nitrified to nitrite and then nitrate by Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter. Denitrification returns N₂ to the atmosphere.

subject: Biology
text_content: Ecological succession: primary succession occurs on bare substrate (no soil), beginning with pioneer species (lichens, mosses). Secondary succession occurs where the ecosystem is disturbed but soil remains. Climax community is the stable end state.

subject: Biology
text_content: Food webs and energy flow: only ~10% of energy is transferred between trophic levels (the 10% rule / ecological efficiency). Energy is lost as heat. Producers → Primary consumers → Secondary consumers → Tertiary consumers.

subject: Physics
text_content: Polytropic processes follow PV^n = constant. Special cases: n=0 isobaric, n=1 isothermal, n=γ adiabatic, n=∞ isochoric. The work done in a polytropic process is W = (P₂V₂ − P₁V₁)/(1 − n).

subject: Physics
text_content: Polarisation of light: transverse waves can be polarised; longitudinal cannot. Malus's Law: I = I₀ cos²θ, where θ is the angle between the polariser and analyser axes.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: The Cannizzaro reaction occurs for aldehydes without α-hydrogens. One molecule is oxidised (→ carboxylic acid) and another is reduced (→ alcohol) in the presence of concentrated NaOH. It is a disproportionation reaction.

subject: Chemistry
text_content: Ionic product of water K_w = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 10⁻¹⁴ at 25°C. pH = −log[H⁺]. For pure water, [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ M, so pH = 7. K_w increases with temperature, so hot neutral water has pH < 7.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: The epsilon-delta definition of a limit: lim_(x→a) f(x) = L if for every ε > 0, there exists δ > 0 such that |x − a| < δ implies |f(x) − L| < ε.

subject: Mathematics
text_content: Euler's totient function φ(n) counts integers from 1 to n that are coprime to n. For prime p, φ(p) = p − 1. Euler's theorem: a^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n) when gcd(a, n) = 1.

subject: Biology
text_content: Epigenetics refers to heritable changes in gene expression that do not involve changes to the DNA sequence. Mechanisms include DNA methylation (typically silences genes) and histone modification (acetylation activates; methylation can activate or silence).

subject: Biology
text_content: RNA interference (RNAi): double-stranded RNA is cleaved by the enzyme Dicer into small interfering RNAs (siRNAs, ~21 nt). siRNAs are incorporated into RISC (RNA-induced silencing complex), which degrades complementary mRNA, silencing gene expression.

text_content: Euler's totient function φ(n) counts integers from 1 to n that are coprime to n. For prime p, φ(p) = p − 1. Euler's theorem: a^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n) when gcd(a, n) = 1.
